publicTrace: Base rate reference class: The SPM child poverty rate has ranged from 12.4% to 17.0% in the post-2021 expanded-CTC era (2022–2024), with the 2024 published rate at 13.4% and the post-expansion average near 13.2%. Year-over-year changes have been modest (−0.3 pp in the most recent period), anchoring the reference class tightly around 12–15%.

Point estimate mechanism: The calibrated point estimate of 13.0% blends the PolicyEngine current-law prior (13.0%, weight 0.55), the post-expansion Census SPM history average (13.2%, weight 0.35), and the latest published 2024 rate (13.4%, weight 0.10), with a small macro adjustment of −0.05 pp. This yields a weighted center near 13.0%.

Upside risk (above interval): If SNAP or Medicaid administrative churn increases, EITC take-up falls, or housing cost burdens rise faster than SPM thresholds adjust, the rate could exceed 14.5%. A recession or significant job loss in 2025 would also push the rate higher.

Downside risk (below interval): If refundable tax credit expansions, enhanced SNAP benefits, or strong wage growth for low-income families materialize beyond current-law baselines, the rate could fall below 11.5%. Disconfirming scenario: a surprise legislative expansion of the CTC in 2025 could push the rate well below the interval.

Uncertainty widening: The PolicyEngine input is a stored prior, not a fresh microsimulation; the Census SPM tables page was reachable but no machine-readable child-poverty series was parsed. This data-path incompleteness warrants wider tails than a fully-verified microsimulation would support. The 80% interval is set at 11.5%–14.5% (±1.5 pp asymmetrically around 13.0%).

Distribution shape: The CDF is constructed as a near-linear ramp from 10% to 16% support, with the bulk of probability mass concentrated between 11.5% and 14.5%, reflecting the tight post-expansion historical range and the blended point estimate. Tails are thin but non-negligible given policy and sampling uncertainty.
assumptions: PolicyEngine current-law prior of 13.0% is treated as a credible but unverified microsimulation seed, not a confirmed fresh run for 2025.
Post-expansion SPM child poverty history (2022–2024) is the primary reference class; pre-2022 rates are excluded as structurally different due to the temporary CTC expansion.

No major new federal legislation affecting child poverty (e.g., CTC expansion, SNAP cuts) is assumed to have been enacted and fully implemented in 2025 beyond current law as of the PolicyEngine check.
ASEC sampling variance for the SPM child poverty rate is approximately ±0.3–0.5 pp at the 90% confidence level, contributing to distributional uncertainty.
Geographic housing cost adjustments and medical out-of-pocket expense volatility in the SPM are assumed to follow recent trends without structural breaks.
dataCaveats: The Census SPM data tables page was fetched successfully but no machine-readable child poverty series was parsed; the 13.4% (2024) and historical series are prototype seeds, not live API values.
The PolicyEngine prior (13.0%) reflects a stored current-law estimate, not a fresh server-side microsimulation for calendar year 2025; actual policy implementation details may differ.
SPM estimates are sensitive to medical out-of-pocket expense imputations and geographic housing adjustments, which can introduce volatility not captured in the blended point estimate.
The 2025 SPM release is expected in September 2026; any interim policy changes (e.g., SNAP rule changes, Medicaid unwinding effects) occurring in 2025 are not fully modeled here.
drivers: PolicyEngine current-law microsimulation prior anchoring the point estimate at 13.0%
Post-expansion Census SPM child poverty history (2022–2024 average ~13.2%)
SNAP, EITC, and refundable tax credit generosity under current law
SPM threshold adjustments for housing costs and medical out-of-pocket expenses
Labor market conditions and wage growth for low-income families with children in 2025
